slides.title: On or off
slides.text: Inside a computer, everything is kept as tiny switches that are on or off. Each switch is called a bit.
slides.alt: Five switches worth 16, 8, 4, 2 and 1: the 4 and the 1 are on, and the total reads 5.

focus.cue: Each switch is a bit: on or off

slides.title: Counting with bits
slides.text: Counting with bits is called binary. Five switches worth 16, 8, 4, 2 and 1 can make any number from 0 to 31.
slides.alt: Read the cards: 16 off, 8 off, 4 on, 2 on, 1 off. Which number do the switches make: 6, 42 or 2?

slides.title: Make the number 5
slides.text: Turn on the switches that add up to your number. 4 and 1 make 5.
slides.alt: Five switches worth 16, 8, 4, 2 and 1: the 4 and the 1 are on, and the total reads 5.

slides.title: Pictures are dots
slides.text: A picture on a screen is made of tiny dots called pixels. The software tells the screen which pixels to light, and in which color.
slides.alt: A picture as a grid of pixels: rows 1 to 3 are copied, dark where the row says 1, light where it says 0.

focus.cue: A picture is a grid of dots: pixels
Dark where the row says 1, light where it says 0

slides.title: Where does a photo live?
slides.text: The screen only shows a photo. The photo is kept in storage as bits, so it is still there when the tablet is off. Tap it: the touch sensor feels it, the processor gets the bits from storage, the screen lights the pixels.
slides.alt: You take a photo and switch the tablet off. Where is the photo? In storage, kept as bits; gone forever; on the dark screen.

focus.cue: The tablet is off: where is the photo?

words.means: one tiny switch: on (1) or off (0)
one tiny dot of a picture
where bits are kept, even with the power off

slides.title: Gizmo's piece lights up
slides.text: Gizmo's piece flies home: four of four. The pieces are ready, but the Spark is not back yet. One last unit is about the people who use technology. Finish it, and you put the Spark together.

slides.title: Your mission
slides.text: Open Inside the Machine at Bits & Pixels and finish all 5 levels. Flip the switches to make each number or letter.
slides.alt: Five switches worth 16, 8, 4, 2 and 1: the 4 and the 1 are on, and the total reads 5.
